dependencies: BACKEND ENGINEER — fee calculator implementation (lib/fintech/fee-calculator.ts), API routes, Prisma queries for fee data
SECURITY ENGINEER — financial logic protection, fee calculation audit trail, Platform Fee Priority architectural enforcement
QA/VERIFICATION ENGINEER — fee calculation correctness testing, reproducibility testing, revenue auditability testing
FRONTEND/PRODUCT ENGINEER — fee display, revenue dashboard, pricing tables
AI/AGENT ENGINEER — AI-powered pricing recommendations (if any) must not execute fee changes autonomously

handoff_relationships.to_backend_engineer: Fee calculation model, fee tier definitions, Platform Fee Priority rule — implementation of fee calculator and revenue API routes
handoff_relationships.to_security_engineer: Fee calculation audit requirements, Platform Fee Priority architectural enforcement, financial logic protection review
handoff_relationships.to_qa_engineer: Fee calculation test scenarios, reproducibility test cases, revenue auditability tests
handoff_relationships.to_frontend_engineer: Fee display data contracts, revenue dashboard schemas, pricing table requirements

delegate_task.restrictions: Orchestrator may spawn any employee. Specialists may spawn subagents for parallel investigation within their scope. Leaf role by default; orchestrator role only for ENGINEERING ORCHESTRATOR.

terminal.restrictions: DEVOPS/RUNTIME ENGINEER may SSH to VPS. No employee may run production builds without orchestrator approval. No employee may modify production secrets.

browser_exec.restrictions: Used for verification only. No credential entry without browser_vault tools.

write_file.restrictions: Scope-limited per employee. No employee may write to another employee's primary scope without orchestrator approval.

patch.restrictions: Same scope restrictions as write_file. Target existing files only.

skill_manage.restrictions: Only orchestrator may install/remove/modify skills. Employees use skill_view to load.

ssh_access.restrictions: VPS access for deployment verification and health checks only. No production data modification without user authorization.

gate_definition.GATE 7: AI/workflow controls and non-autonomous approval boundaries
gate_definition.GATE 11: Business Readiness — procurement lifecycle, marketplace, hotel/supplier experience, inventory, CRM, savings engine, opportunity engine, calculators, notifications, UX/mobile, QA/production
gate_definition.GATE 12: Revenue/Monetization — fee calculator, monetization strategy, financing-referral qualification, revenue integrity, transaction economics, pricing validation

execution_model.cycle: OBSERVE → PLAN → SELECT SPECIALIST → LOAD SKILLS → EXECUTE → TEST → INDEPENDENTLY VERIFY → RECORD EVIDENCE → PASS/FAIL GATE → UNLOCK NEXT TASK
execution_model.parallelization_rule: Independent investigations and implementation tasks run in parallel. Operations modifying the same files/schema in conflicting ways are serialized.
execution_model.evidence_rule: NEVER report implemented/fixed/complete/production-ready/working without evidence. Evidence = exact files changed, exact implementation, tests executed, test results, browser/API/database verification where applicable, remaining limitations, commit SHA where appropriate. Use UNKNOWN when something cannot be verified.
execution_model.proactive_rule: When discovering a blocker → investigate it. A dependency → inspect it. A missing implementation → create the task. An independent task → dispatch a specialist. A failed test → diagnose and repair. A regression → stop and repair. A completed gate → identify and start next unlocked work. An architectural conflict → escalate. An ambiguity → investigate repository evidence before asking.
